That can't be right. cgroup.type can only be one of "domain", "domain threaded", "threaded", or "domain threaded". Wait — actually, the possible values for cgroup.type are: "domain", "domain threaded", "threaded". "domain threaded" is valid! From the kernel docs:

> cgroup.type: This file contains one of the following values:
> - "domain": the cgroup is a domain cgroup
> - "domain threaded": the cgroup is a domain cgroup that allows threads
> - "threaded": the cgroup is a threaded cgroup (no processes, only threads)

So "domain threaded" means a domain cgroup that has threaded members — i.e., the cgroup.threads flag was set to 1. This matches runc's error "cannot enter cgroupv2 with domain controllers -- it is in threaded mode".

So the write to cgroup.threads succeeded with rc=0, but the mode didn't change (still "domain threaded"). That's because... you can only clear threaded mode when there are no threads in the cgroup and no domain controllers enabled in the subtree? Actually: "The cgroup.threads file can only be written to when there are no processes in the cgroup and no controllers enabled in the subtree." Let me recall the exact rule:

From cgroup v2 docs:
> **cgroup.threads**
> A cgroup can enable threaded mode by writing 1 to this file... This file is only writable if the cgroup has no member processes (cgroup.procs is empty), and only if no domain controller is enabled in the subtree (subtree_control contains no domain controllers)...

The actual rule: to disable threaded mode, there must be no processes in the cgroup, and no domain controller can be enabled in the subtree. Also, to enable it, you need to first move all processes out.

The root cgroup has 1656 processes (PID 1, dockerd, etc.), so it can't be cleared. And /sys/fs/cgroup/docker also has processes in it (dockerd 4, containerd 45, buildkit, etc.).
